rules.statement: Derive an approximate developmental stage (yearsUntilGraduation = graduation_year - currentYear) from data ORYN already collects; expose it as a non-binding display default a student can override, never as a hard eligibility gate or a claim of precision it doesn't have. Degrade to 'insufficient data for timing context' for education_stage='other' or curriculum='other' rather than silently defaulting to one country's grade system.

Stage (years until graduation) determines WHAT KIND of recommendation is appropriate; the student's own time budget determines HOW MUCH/HOW BIG. Never let a tight time budget silently substitute a breadth-type recommendation for a depth-type one -- if nothing depth-appropriate fits, say so explicitly rather than swapping category.

A student outside the typical phase pattern for their stage is not automatically a gap. Distinguish objective time-remaining from implied deficiency: a Phase-1 student with genuine early depth should not be pushed toward artificial breadth; a Phase-2 student who is broad due to a recent, legitimate interest shift should have that context surfaced, not be penalized as if the shift never happened.

Treat 'Computer Science' as an umbrella, not a single skill -- competitive-programming-style algorithmic problem-solving and building/shipping user-facing products are both legitimately 'CS' but develop measurably different things.

When counseling a CS-interested student, distinguish at minimum three evidence types -- sustained independent build (execution_project_depth), algorithmic competition (quantitative/algorithmic reasoning under contest conditions), and time-boxed hackathon/team build (rapid-build + teamwork) -- rather than treating 'did something CS-related' as one undifferentiated signal.

'I like math' may mean enjoying proof/abstraction (pure track), applied problem-solving with formulas (applied track), or analyzing data (statistics track) -- these predict different downstream fits and should not be treated as one undifferentiated signal.

A stated interest in 'physics' or 'chemistry' should be probed for which pole a student actually enjoys -- theoretical/mathematical problem-solving vs. hands-on experimental work reward different exploration experiences.
'Biology' spans wet-lab/bench work, field/ecological work, and computational biology -- probing which a student means matters as much here as for computing/mathematics.

A biology major is necessary for essentially no clinical health profession in most systems -- pre-med 'requirements' are typically specific courses, not a mandated major. Must be stated explicitly to counteract a common real-world misconception.

'Engineering' as a stated interest is at least as broad as 'Computer Science' or 'Biology' -- a student should sample more than one of mechanical/civil/aerospace/electrical before narrowing, since they involve meaningfully different day-to-day work despite a shared first-year curriculum.

PE-equivalent licensure necessity varies substantially by role AND industry, not just by engineering subfield -- civil engineers stamping public infrastructure plans are the clearest necessity case; many ME/EE/AE industry roles (esp. aerospace/defense, tech-adjacent EE) practice career-long without one. A specific student's situation should be checked against target industry/employer expectations, not inferred from subfield alone.

Biomedical engineering is not a subset of 'pre-med' and should not be counseled as one -- it is an engineering discipline whose graduates mostly go into engineering/industry/research roles, not clinical practice. A student wanting to become a physician does not need a biomedical engineering degree. (Generalizes RULE-COUNSEL-042 to this field.)

Economics is a genuinely quantitative social science -- a student drawn to it purely for real-world relevance (news/policy) without appetite for the underlying statistics/econometrics is a real, worth-surfacing mismatch signal (a counseling conversation topic, not a disqualification).

Entrepreneurship is about originating and testing a new venture; general business/management study is about operating and improving an existing one. A strong management-track profile is not automatically evidence of entrepreneurial capability, and vice versa.

DECA/FBLA-style competitive-simulation participation demonstrates applied business-scenario reasoning and communication skill, but is NOT entrepreneurship evidence in the 'originate and test a real venture' sense -- it is a simulation, not the operation of a real business. Do not conflate the two evidence types.

'Environmental science' and 'sustainability' are not the same activity profile -- a student drawn to fieldwork/conservation and one drawn to sustainability policy/business practice are both legitimately in this family but benefit from different exploration experiences.

Never state a probability of admission/success/outcome without a validated statistical model backing it -- restates the founder spec's non-negotiable #5 as an explainability rule for why[]/warnings[] text specifically.

Never let a ProfileGap (Oryn's own developmental judgment) imply a university 'requires' addressing it -- only a sourced, per-university RequirementEvaluationSummary is allowed to make a requirement-style claim.

Never hide low confidence behind confident-sounding language -- a confidence:'low' recommendation must lead with the data gap itself, not bury it in a trailing warning the student might not read as carefully.

Distinguish 'verified information' from 'Oryn analysis' in the actual RENDERED text a student sees, not just internally in the data model -- externally-sourced content (a requirement's own reasoning) should be visually/textually distinguishable from Oryn's own developmental judgment.

A deprioritize/avoid_for_now recommendation's why[] must always include a redirect -- either the specific higher-value gap it's implicitly weighed against, or an honest statement that it's simply not currently a priority given time constraints -- never a bare 'this is low value' with no comparison point.

Every piece of reasoning this research package contributes must enter why[]/warnings[] as a parameterized template string keyed to a real structured fact -- never as a place where an LLM is asked to 'explain this in your own words' for the deterministic pipeline. Richer nuance that doesn't fit a short template belongs in the optional LLM narration layer's input context, still wrapped in the existing untrusted-data boundary -- never a relaxation of the deterministic pipeline's no-free-text rule.

Never present a specific named opportunity/program sourced only from secondary/aggregator discovery as a confirmed, current, verified offering to a student -- it must first pass through ORYN's actual opportunity-acquisition/verification pipeline. This research package documents pathway TYPES, not a verified directory.

rules.statement: Never infer a student's aptitude, interest, or fit for any field from a demographic attribute (nationality, gender, school type, socioeconomic signal, or any similar proxy).
rules.note: Directly restates the mission brief's own explicit 'what Oryn must not do' list verbatim; minted here because neither branch had numbered it explicitly yet, though both branches' actual document content is already consistent with it throughout.

rules.statement: Never present one career family as objectively 'better' than another (e.g., by salary or prestige) independent of the specific student's own stated interests/goals.

Never equate a career family's aggregate popularity or labor-market growth rate with a claim about a specific student's likely fit or success in it -- every BLS growth statistic cited across this package's family docs is an aggregate US labor-market data point, never a claim about an individual student's prospects.

Where a UK-facing student needs career-outlook grounding, prefer National Careers Service job profiles over BLS/O*NET -- they are the UK's own official equivalent, not a secondary source, and salary/qualification framing does not transfer across countries even when the occupation name is identical.

Turkey's TMMOB chamber-registration/title-protection system is structurally distinct from BOTH the US PE system (voluntary-until-triggered-by-specific-practice) and the UK CEng system (institution-administered chartered status layered on top of an unrestricted base right to practice) -- a Turkey-target engineering student should not have US/UK licensure framing applied to them by default.

Never apply US-holistic-admissions-derived reasoning (depth-over-breadth, extracurricular signaling, redundancy/saturation logic) with the same directness to a student targeting an admissions system with a fundamentally different structure -- e.g. Turkey's exam-score-dominated YKS placement (where academics is doing nearly all the admissions work and the other 8 ProfileDimensions matter for real development but should not be framed as admissions-relevant), or the UK's UCAS system (which weights subject-relevant super-curricular engagement over general extracurricular breadth more heavily than US holistic review does). Oryn's developmental framing remains valid regardless of geography; its ADMISSIONS-RELEVANCE framing must be geography-conditional. Assessed as the single highest-leverage open item this whole research package surfaced (verified independently by both sessions).
rules.note: Originally surfaced by the peer session's persona-testing pass, independently verified by this session via direct ÖSYM/YKS and UCAS sourcing. Highest-priority item for any future continuation of this research.

rules.statement: Unlike DECA/FBLA-style simulated-scenario competitions (RULE-COUNSEL-048), UK's Young Enterprise Company Programme genuinely clears the 'real, tested venture' bar for entrepreneurship evidence -- real company, real bank account, real customers, not a simulation. A UK student's participation should be evaluated against the founder spec's 'idea -> built -> tested' ladder, not treated as equivalent to a DECA/FBLA placement.
